defects: Uses `List.count p l` where `List.count` expects an element of type `α` for equality-counting, not a predicate `p : α → Bool` — this is a type mismatch/misuse; the intended function is `List.countP p l`

Even interpreting it as countP, 'count ≤ 1' counts occurrences of matching elements in the list, which is stronger than gold's `{x ∈ l₁ | p x}.Subsingleton` (a Set condition) — gold allows the same satisfying value to appear multiple times in the list, the produced hypothesis would forbid that
Conclusion uses `List.head (List.filter p l)` but `List.head` requires a proof argument that the list is nonempty (`l ≠ []`); as written this does not typecheck

Even if `head?`/`head!` were intended, the conclusion no longer mirrors gold's behavior in the no-match case: `find?` returns `none` on both sides when no element satisfies p, whereas `head`/`head!` on an empty filtered list is undefined or a junk value, changing the theorem's meaning for that case
Implicit arguments `p`, `l₁`, `l₂` in gold are made explicit in the produced statement (minor stylistic deviation)
